root_cause: The _onInputBlur handler uses a 100ms setTimeout to hide the date picker. During this delay, the picker remains visible in the DOM and can trap focus. When Tab moves focus from #checkin to #guests, the blur handler's pending timeout fires, hides the picker, and focus returns to #checkin.
repair_strategy: Remove the setTimeout in _onInputBlur so the picker hides immediately when focus leaves the field (unless a picker button interaction is in progress, tracked by the _c flag set in _onMouseDown). Also update _onInputFocus to clear any pending timeout using clearTimeout instead of the non-existent sto.clear method.
expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key navigation from the date input (#checkin) to the next form field (#guests) works correctly without focus returning to the date field, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Immediate hide on blur could theoretically interfere with picker button clicks if blur fires before click, but the _c flag (set on mousedown) prevents hide during picker interaction.
The blurFieldOnSelect option still calls field.blur() after hide, which is harmless since focus has already moved.
verification_requirements: The journey test passes: Tab from #checkin moves focus to #guests and keeps it there (focus assertion passes).
Form data for checkin (2026-12-04) and guests (2) are both correctly set.
Regression guard: pointer paging months keeps keyboard focus in the date field.
